misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program CekBilanganPrima
kamus
  n, i : integer
  prima : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  if n >= 1 then
    prima <- true
    i <- 2
    if i < n div 2 then
      if n mod i == 0 then
        prima <- false
      else
        i <- i + 1
      endif
    endif
  else
    prima <- false
  endif
  output(prima)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for-loop with an if-statement, believing it will behave like a while-loop. They initialize i=2 and use 'if i < num//2:' expecting it to repeatedly execute while the condition holds true. Inside, they increment i (i = i + 1) thinking this will allow the if-statement to check the next value automatically. From the student's perspective, this should check all values from 2 to num//2 just like the original loop did. However, the if-statement only executes once, so the function only checks divisibility by 2 and then returns True for any number not divisible by 2 (incorrectly marking composites like 9, 15, 21, etc. as prime).
